title: DistDF: Time-series Forecasting Needs Joint-distribution Wasserstein Alignment
claim: Raw labels show strong conditional autocorrelation that biases standard objectives; decorrelating transforms only partially remove it, leaving residual dependence.
layout: 3 heatmap panels in a row, shared colorbars, lower-triangular matrices
description: Three side-by-side lower-triangle-masked correlation heatmaps, each 192×192 with axes ticks from 0 to 192, rendered in purple shades with a discrete colorbar from 0.000 to 1.000 (log-like bins 0.001, 0.010, 0.100). Panel (a), Raw labels, is densely dark purple with banded, wavy diagonal stripes, showing strong correlation among label steps. Panel (b), FreDF components, is much lighter with scattered speckle and faint diagonal lines plus a white-outlined inset square near the upper right. Panel (c), Time-o1 components, is also pale, with a few darker dots concentrated near the top-left and along the diagonal. The eye goes first to the dark raw-label panel, then compares it against the two lighter panels. Captions below each panel, with vertical black dividers between panels.
caption: The conditional correlation of label components given x, where the forecast length is set to T = 192. The correlation matrices are computed for the raw labels (a), the frequency components in FreDF (b) (Wang et al., 2025d) and the principal components in Time-o1 (c) (Wang et al., 2025c).
abstract: Training time-series forecasting models requires aligning the conditional distribution of model forecasts with that of the label sequence. The standard direct forecast (DF) approach resorts to minimizing the conditional negative log-likelihood, typically estimated by the mean squared error. However, this estimation proves biased when the label sequence exhibits autocorrelation. In this paper, we propose DistDF, which achieves alignment by minimizing a distributional discrepancy between the conditional distributions of forecast and label sequences. Since such conditional discrepancies are difficult to estimate from finite time-series observations, we introduce a joint-distribution Wasserstein discrepancy for time-series forecasting, which provably upper bounds the conditional discrepancy of interest. The proposed discrepancy is tractable, differentiable, and readily compatible with gradient-based optimization. Extensive experiments show that DistDF improves diverse forecasting models and achieves leading performance. Code is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/DistDF-F66B.
